t.6.18.1: But I shall describe to you, as you look on, those leaders of the troops who, showing their valour for Rāghava's sake, do not hold their own lives dear.
t.6.18.2: He of terrible deeds, whose glossy hairs, deeply dark, cling to his tail, spread out and copper-red, yellow, pale and white.
t.6.18.3: Held aloft, they shine like the rays of the sun, and they are dragged along upon the earth; this leader of a troop is named Hara.
t.6.18.4: He whom they follow from behind by hundreds and then by thousands, gathered together, lifting up trees, intent on scaling Laṅkā.
t.6.18.5: This one, with a thousand crores of monkeys of great might, longs to conquer you in battle, O conqueror of enemy cities.
t.6.18.6: Those whom you see standing there like great dark clouds, resembling black collyrium, are of true valour in battle.
t.6.18.7: Heroes whose weapons are claws and fangs, fierce in their wrath and fearsome to behold, countless and beyond all description, like the farther shore of the ocean.
t.6.18.8: Whatever bears there are, dwelling in the mountains, in rugged places and by the rivers, these exceedingly fierce bears, O king, are advancing toward you.
t.6.18.9: Standing in their midst, O king, is one of fearsome eyes and fearsome appearance, surrounded on all sides like Parjanya by the rain-clouds.
t.6.18.10: This troop-leader named Dhūmra, lord of all the bears, dwells on Ṛkṣavant, the best of mountains, drinking the waters of the Narmadā.
t.6.18.11: But look at this one, like a mountain, his younger brother, equal to his brother in form but surpassing him in valour.
t.6.18.12: This one here is the one named Jāmbavān, a commander over great commanders of troops; he is calm and obedient to his elders, yet in battles he is unforbearing.
t.6.18.13: By this wise Jāmbavant very great help was rendered to Śakra in the war between the gods and the asuras, and many boons were obtained by him.
t.6.18.14: Climbing up, they hurl down from the mountain peaks rocks as vast as great clouds, enormous in form, and they do not shrink from death.
t.6.18.15: In his army roam many hairy ones, resembling rākṣasas and piśācas, possessing the splendour of fire.
t.6.18.16: But he whom all the monkeys gaze upon, standing there enraged as though about to leap, the leader of the leaders of troops standing firm, is this one.
t.6.18.17: O king, this lord of monkeys waits upon the thousand-eyed one with his forces. Endowed with might, this troop leader is named Rambha.
t.6.18.18: He who, as he goes along, brushes with his flank a mountain standing a yojana away, and who likewise, rising upward with his body, reaches the height of a yojana.
t.6.18.19: He, than whom no finer form is found among four-footed creatures, is the renowned one named Saṃnādana, the grandfather of the vānaras.
t.6.18.20: He, the wise one, who once gave battle to Śakra on the battlefield and did not meet with defeat, is this leader of the leaders of troops, whose prowess, when he strides forth in valor, is like that of Śakra.
t.6.18.21: This one was born long ago of a Gandharva maiden by Kṛṣṇavartman, the god of fire, during the war between the devas and the asuras, to bring aid to the dwellers of heaven.
t.6.18.22: He in whose realm King Vaiśravaṇa frequents the Jambū tree, he who is king over the lords of mountains, haunts of many Kiṃnaras.
t.6.18.24: Surrounded by a thousand koṭis of monkeys, he has arrived here; this very one hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own army.
t.6.18.23: O lord of the rākṣasas, there, in the place that ever gives your brother the joy of recreation, dwells this glorious and mighty bull among monkeys, the troop-leader named Krathana, who never boasts in battle.
t.6.18.25: He who roams along the Gaṅgā, terrifying the leaders of the elephant herds, remembering the ancient enmity between elephants and monkeys.
t.6.18.26: This one is a leader of troops and a guide, dwelling in mountain caves, the foremost of the army of monkeys; they went along the river Haimavatī.
t.6.18.27: Resorting to Uśīrabīja, a mountain like Mandara, that best of monkeys takes his delight, just as Śakra himself does in heaven.
t.6.18.28: A thousand times a hundred thousand follow him. This, O king, is the troop-leader named Pramāthin, hard to withstand.
t.6.18.29: He whom you see there, like a cloud tossed up by the wind, wheeling about again and again, where this thick dust rises,
t.6.18.30: These dreadful, black-faced golāṅgūlas of great might, a hundred hundred-thousands in number, have indeed seen the building of the bridge.
t.6.18.31: Surrounding the swift golāṅgūla, the troop-leader named Gavākṣa, they advance to crush Laṅkā with their might.
t.6.18.33: By whose radiance the beasts and birds forever shine, taking on its very hue; whose plateau the great-souled great sages never forsake.
t.6.18.32: There, where the trees bearing fruits that fulfil every desire are frequented by bees, stands the mountain, radiant with a hue like the sun's, around which the sun moves in its circuit.
t.6.18.34: There, on the lovely golden mountain, this resplendent one takes his delight: the troop-leader named Kesarī, foremost among the chiefs of the vānaras.
t.6.18.35: There are sixty thousand lovely golden mountains, and in their midst stands the best of mountains, just as you, O sinless one, stand foremost among the rākṣasas.
t.6.18.36: There, on that excellent mountain, dwell these monkeys, tawny and white, copper-faced and honey-brown, whose weapons are their sharp fangs and claws.
t.6.18.37: Like lions with four fangs, like tigers hard to approach, all of them are equal to fire and resemble blazing venomous serpents.
t.6.18.38: With very long, curled tails, they resembled rutting elephants; like great mountains in size, they roared like great thunderclouds.
t.6.18.39: And this mighty one standing in their midst is their lord, who is renowned on earth by the name Śatabali, O king. This very one hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own army.
t.6.18.40: The monkeys Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Nala and Nīla are each surrounded by ten crores of troops.
t.6.18.41: Likewise, there are other foremost vānaras dwelling on the Vindhya mountain, swift in their stride, who cannot be counted because of their great number.
t.6.18.42: All of them, O great king, are of mighty power, and all have bodies like great mountains. Every one of them is able, in a single moment, to make the earth a place whose mountains lie shattered and scattered.
